source.ranges: ISFG minimum range from FSSG v6.1 (STRidER; distributed as FSSG_v6-1_beta.xlsx), accessed 2026-09-28 (SHA-256 acf2fa7f16e911474152e52654e77c160d7b34f3d7a72e158def303fff9449e1, identical to the copy used), GRCh38; inputs on the GRCh38 forward strand, BED strand '+'
source.refseq: GRCh38 no-alt analysis set (NCBI, local fasta via STRNAMING_FASTA_REFERENCE). Cross-check: when STRNaming reads GRCh38 from the Ensembl REST cache instead, it returns identical names for all 1591 STRbase sequences and for the 62 reference names the file held when that check was run (69 now).
source.reference: Name of the GRCh38 reference sequence over the ISFG minimum range. Verified: the CE in the name equals the FSSG CE and the structure fits one of STRidER's canonical bracketing templates.
source.strbase: Each STRbase Variant Allele sequence is windowed to the ISFG minimum range with flank anchors from the FSSG full-range sequence, then named. A name is kept only when its CE equals the STRbase allele designation. status: ok | held (CE mismatch, kept for manual review, no name published) | not_covered (the STRbase sequence does not span the ISFG minimum range). Names are published only for status ok (see counts).
source.alignment: strbase[marker][i] matches markerData[marker].sequences[i]; h = first 10 hex of SHA-1 of the uppercase sequence (checked by lib/strnaming-names.test.ts).
source.isfg: Sequence over the ISFG minimum range that produced the name: the STRbase sequence windowed with scripts/strnaming-window-strbase.py (FSSG flank anchors), the exact input to STRNaming 1.2.1 with the range in 'ranges'. Present for ok and held rows; absent for not_covered. Regenerated 2026-10-02: all 1569 published names reproduce from it.
source.heldCe: For held rows, the CE in the name STRNaming gives for 'isfg'; it differs from the STRbase allele designation, so no name is published.
